at1SemanticsUnchanged.evidence: git diff of compareImages: the only change to the @1 path is hoisting the six overWhite() calls into named locals (identical values, identical composite-over-white, identical Math.round) and replacing three sequential `if (dX > maxChannelDelta)` updates with one `pixelMax` that is the max of the same three. changedPixels still increments on `dr !== 0 || dg !== 0 || db !== 0`; totalDelta still accumulates (dr+dg+db)/3; changedPixelRatio, commonAreaRatio, meanAbsoluteRgbDelta, maxChannelDelta and renderDiffImage are untouched. smoke-reconstruction-qa.ts's 15 screenshot-metric checks (which pin @1) all PASS.

at16IsMaxChannel.evidence: const pixelMax = max(dr, dg, db); if (pixelMax >= CHANGED_PIXEL_AMPLITUDE_THRESHOLD) changedPixelsAt16++ — a per-pixel MAX, not a sum and not an average. Threshold is an exported constant = 16, comparison is >= (boundary 16 counts, 15 does not; the suite pins both).

dE76ReferenceCheck.method: tmp/wr285b/verify-qa/de76.ts — an independent reimplementation written by the verifier (exact CIE constants: knee (6/29)^3 = 0.0088564517, slope (1/3)(29/6)^2 = 7.787037, offset 4/29) compared against the repo's srgbToLab + deltaE76

mathAudit.srgbToLinear: PASS — 256-entry LUT, knee at 0.04045, else ((c+0.055)/1.055)^2.4, divisor 12.92. Correct sRGB EOTF. Safe to LUT because both sides are composited over white by overWhite(), which Math.rounds to an integer 0..255, so every index is in range (verified: overWhite can never produce <0, >255 or a non-integer).
mathAudit.labF: ACCEPTABLE — uses the legacy CIE approximation t > 0.008856 ? cbrt(t) : 7.787t + 16/116 rather than the exact (6/29)^3 / (1/3)(29/6)^2 / 4/29 form. Measured divergence from the exact form is <= 2.6e-6 ΔE and only in the sub-knee (near-black) region. Not a defect at the 2.3 / 10 thresholds in use.
mathAudit.deltaE76: PASS — plain Euclidean distance in L*a*b*, no weighting.

dE76ReferenceCheck.referenceValueNote: The suite asserts against published EasyRGB triples (red L* 53.2408 ± 0.01). The repo's 4-decimal matrix and 95.047 white give 53.2329 — inside the tolerance by 0.0021. Passing but tight; a future constants refresh could break that assertion without any real regression. Same for 'grey 200 vs 208 ≈ 2.92 ± 0.05' where the actual value is 2.8781 (margin 0.008).

adversarial.nanScan: No path produces NaN or Infinity. tmp/wr285b/verify-qa/edge.ts exercised zero-overlap, height mismatch, fully transparent vs opaque white, and 50% alpha; every numeric field in every ImageComparison was finite. overWhite() provably returns an integer in [0,255] for any (0..255, 0..255) input, so the SRGB_TO_LINEAR LUT index is always in range and the non-null assertions cannot yield undefined.
adversarial.dimensionMismatch: Metrics are computed over min(width) × min(height) only, never resized; widthDelta/heightDelta and commonAreaRatio report the shortfall. Row indexing uses each image's own stride (rowA = y * a.width * 4), which is correct for differing widths. Verified: a 10×20 vs 10×10 pair reports heightDelta -10, commonAreaRatio 0.5 and 0 changed pixels over the overlap.
adversarial.zeroOverlapReadsAsZero: When overlapPixels === 0 every ratio and mean is guarded to 0 and deltaE76Max is round4(0) = 0 — i.e. a pair with no overlap reads numerically as 'identical'. This mirrors the pre-existing @1 behaviour exactly (changedPixelRatio was already 0 there) and commonAreaRatio 0 discloses it, so it is not a new hazard, but a reader who looks only at deltaE76Mean could be misled. Worth naming in any report that consumes these fields.
adversarial.alpha: Both sides are composited over white with the SAME unchanged overWhite() before differencing, and ΔE76 is computed on the composited values, so alpha can never be read as a colour difference. Verified: fully transparent garbage RGB vs opaque white → 0 on every channel; 50% black over white vs white → @1 1.0, @16 1.0, ΔE76 46.8072, all consistent.
adversarial.shortCircuitSoundness: SOUND, no false negatives. ΔE76 is skipped only when pixelMax === 0, which means all three composited channels are bit-identical, which means both sides map to the identical Lab triple, which means ΔE76 is exactly 0 — it cannot exceed 2.3 or 10 and contributes 0 to the mean. The skip changes no reported value.

performance.measured: tmp/wr285b/verify-qa/perf.ts on a 1440×30000 (43.2 M px) pair on this machine
performance.everyPixelDiffers: 2846 ms (the 28.5A @1≈1.0 worst case, where the short-circuit never fires)
performance.assessment: ~10× slowdown in the worst case, but bounded at ~2.8 s per 43 MP pair — affordable. There is no sampling and none is needed at this size. The cost multiplies by pairs, though: 3 pairs × 2 viewports × N pages, so a 10-page run of very tall pages could add on the order of a minute of pure CPU. Not a blocker; worth a timing note on the first real full-site run.
performance.captureCost: Unmeasured on a real site: 30 extra getPropertyValue() calls per element per capture, most of which return a value on every element. The build handoff discloses this.

risks.title: The honesty machinery is proven but INERT in real runs
risks.detail: compareCapturedStyles() and unverifiableFromSpecProperties() are referenced nowhere in src/ outside their own definition file and the barrel export — only scripts/smoke-qa-independence.ts calls them. So on an actual QA run the 30 QA-only properties are captured and then compared against nothing, and no report names them as un-verifiable-from-spec. The blind spot is demonstrably closable but is not yet closed in production. The build handoff discloses this as a follow-up (wire into qa-page.ts), which is honest, but until that lands the user-visible QA behaviour is unchanged except for the pixel channels.

risks.title: The interaction axis is still blind
risks.detail: src/reconstruction-qa/interaction-qa.ts:71 still defines TARGET_STATE_STYLE_PROPERTIES = STYLE_WHITELIST, so open-state style comparison for interactions retains exactly the coupling change 6 removed from page capture. A gradient-knockout or text-shadow difference that appears only in an open state is still invisible. Outside the claimed scope, but it is the same defect in a second place and should be scheduled.

risks.title: Literal-snapshot coupling is a maintenance obligation
risks.detail: QA_STYLE_PROPERTIES is a literal copy of the Observer's 114 properties. When the observer builder adds a property, the suite's 'QA keeps every property the Observer records' check fails until it is copied over. Correctly designed as an alarm rather than silent drift, and the build handoff names it — but it is real ongoing work.

risks.title: Tight reference tolerances in the ΔE76 checks
risks.detail: red L* asserted 53.2408 ± 0.01 against an actual 53.2329 (0.0021 of margin left) and grey200/208 asserted 2.92 ± 0.05 against an actual 2.8781 (0.008 of margin). Both pass, and the underlying math is correct to 1e-6 against an independent exact-constant implementation, but either assertion could flip on a constants cleanup that is not a regression.

risks.title: The CLI headline is still one scalar
risks.detail: src/cli-qa-reconstruction.ts prints only the @1 median (L153, L173). The new channels reach the summary object and worstPages detail, so an operator reading the CLI headline still sees the number 28.5A proved misleading. Disclosed as a follow-up by the builder; noted here because it blunts the change's practical benefit until fixed.
